maya: quick note: new AWQ bring-up (redwood-open-3b-awq-v2) showing intermittent mid-sequence stalls when act-quant >=5 and group_size=48. happens on long-tail convo sims.
eddie: can you paste the exact canary args and a short log snippet?
maya: args: model=redwood-open-3b-awq-v2, actq=5, group_size=48, kv_retention=6000, continuous_batching=true
kai: weird, group_size=48 is non-standard for our allocator. could be alignment with our 64-lane kernels.
maya: log bit:
```
[2026-07-02T03:21:07Z] kv:write idx=0x3a2 slot=19 size=768 delayed=210ms
[2026-07-02T03:21:07Z] awq:actq:pack lane=48 roundoff=2
[2026-07-02T03:21:08Z] decode: stall=5100ms request=rid-f2b
```
leah: any deterministic repro? capture id?
replay-bot: trace captured for thread 1768888888 at 1768888895 -> replay-id: r-1768888895
sam: schedule: run microgrid sweep on ded-gpu-d: group_size=[32,48,64], actq=[4,5], kv_retention=[4096,8192], continuous_batching=[true,false], 250 prompts each. will auto-collect flamegraphs.
eddie: toggle kernel flag `awq.force-aligned-groups=true` to force 64 alignment and see if stalls disappear. also try `--continuous-batching=false` to rule out batch-merge side-effects.
kai: theory: act-quant packing for group_size 48 uses a different packing path that interacts with prefix-merge code; KV index writes can become non-atomic relative to eviction window -> eviction sees partial entry and prunes it -> decoder hits missing prefix -> stall + retries.
maya: quick smoke (50 prompts each) results:
- g32 a4 cb=false kv=8192 -> no stalls, quality delta vs fp16: -0.1 MMLU
- g48 a5 cb=true kv=6000 -> 5 stalls/50, MMLU -2.4 pts, token repetition in 2 prompts
- g64 a5 cb=false kv=8192 -> 1 stall/50, MMLU -0.6
leah: uploading counters and memstats to s3: s3://redwood-dev/awq/176888/replays/r-1768888895-counters.tgz
ops-bot: Canary rollback rule applied: reduce actq to 4 for pool=ded-gpu-d if stall_rate>1% in 5m window
infra-bot: replay job queued -> r-1768888895 running on replay-node-21
sam: next steps: 1) reproduce deterministically via replay and add unit test that races concurrent KV writes and prefix-merge; 2) try forcing aligned groups and re-run grid; 3) bisect runtime kernel changes if deterministic.
eddie: if replay is deterministic we'll run bisection across the AWQ kernels (actq path vs fp16) and compare vectorized stores. maybe a packing store under certain lane counts is not masked correctly.
kai: filing GH issue repo/awq-runtime#578 "non-aligned group packing -> KV partial-write eviction" with attached replay and counters
maya: assigned @kai @leah to triage logging, @eddie to bisect kernels, @sam to run the sweep and coordinate infra. will monitor canary.
leah: started deterministic replay check, will post results and a minimal repro harness to /tmp/awq-repro once done.
maya: thanks all, will update thread after bisection or when we get a solid repro. :mag:
